checks.run: uv run ruff check projects/pigrocrm && uv run ruff format --check projects/pigrocrm
checks.why: Seconds here against a whole round trip in CI. Lint and format are the checks most likely to fail and the cheapest to have failed.
mypy --strict over every Python source root, the hub's three included. The bare `uv run mypy` works because pyproject.toml's [tool.mypy] files list names them.

checks.run: uv run pytest -q -n auto --dist loadfile -m "not slow and not planner" projects/pigrocrm
checks.why: The whole Python suite except the two kinds of check that are not only about the code. `-n auto` because it waits on PostgreSQL far more than it computes: 10m00 -> 3m36 locally, each worker getting its own container from the session fixture.

The fifty-thousand-row corpus: twelve minutes, almost all of it inside PostgreSQL. Serial and never under -n, because every assertion in those two files is about which plan the planner picks and load changes the answer.
Deselected on both CI tiers because a hosted runner picks the other plan (ORB-9). This is the one machine where the assertion means something, so it has to run here or it runs nowhere.
vitest, jsdom, no services. Also the step that writes src/routeTree.gen.ts, which the typecheck below needs and which nothing else generates.

checks.run: pnpm --filter web build && pnpm --filter web exec tsc --noEmit
checks.why: Build before typecheck, always: a bare tsc --noEmit on a clean checkout fails every route file with TS2307 because src/routeTree.gen.ts is gitignored and only a Vite run writes it.
99 assertions on the built and unbuilt text: which tokens each sheet may declare, what each page promises, how the field behaves. No services, about two seconds.

checks.run: pnpm --filter website build && pnpm --filter website exec tsc --noEmit
checks.why: The build is where the palette plugin runs, so a palette that stopped being extractable fails here rather than shipping pages with no colour.

checks.run: uv run ruff check projects/hub && uv run ruff format --check projects/hub
checks.why: The hub's lint and format, seconds here against a round trip in CI.

checks.run: uv run pytest -q projects/hub/packages/core/tests projects/hub/apps/api/tests projects/hub/apps/mcp/tests
checks.why: The hub's whole Python suite: a testcontainers Postgres brought to head by the hub's own migrations, about a minute. mypy is covered by pigrocrm-py-types, whose bare `uv run mypy` reads every source root in [tool.mypy] files.
vitest, jsdom, fetch mocked: the wizard engine, the api client's error shapes, the freelancer wizard end to end.
vite build then tsc --noEmit, the same pair the node gate runs. The route tree is code, so nothing has to be generated first.
Vitest transpiles without typechecking, so unit tests pass on code tsc rejects. This project has noUncheckedIndexedAccess on and the trunk went red that way once (ORB-15).
Playwright against `vite preview` on 4173. Serial because that port is fixed and shared with anything else on this box.

The Playwright suite against a real API and a real Postgres. `serial` because it binds three fixed host ports -- 55433 for its own Postgres, 8000 for the API, 5173 for Vite -- which are hardcoded in projects/pigrocrm/apps/web/scripts/e2e-env.sh rather than read from the environment. On a shared box that is also a collision with anything else holding them, and the script clears :5173 and :8000 before it starts.

checks.run: cd projects/pigrocrm && POSTGRES_PASSWORD=build-only PIGROCRM_JWT_SECRET=build-only-and-long-enough-for-the-validator docker compose build
checks.why: Both images build from the repository-root context they are deployed with. Serial because a docker build saturates the box and this shares it with everyone else's agents.

checks.run: cd projects/website && WEBSITE_WEB_PORT=127.0.0.1:8099 docker compose build
checks.why: The deploy builds this image on a single-core server. Building it here is seconds and it is the only check that reads projects/website/deploy/nginx.conf at all.

checks.run: cd projects/hub && POSTGRES_PASSWORD=build-only-never-used ORBITERS_DATA_DIR=./build-only-never-mounted docker compose -p orbiters build
checks.why: The one project whose images were verified on no tier before the trunk: ci.yml builds them on push only, so a broken Dockerfile here reached main before anything said so. `-p orbiters` because that is the project name the deploy passes (docs/adding-a-project.md section 7) and the name decides the image tags. Serial for the same reason as the other two: a docker build saturates the box.

The other half of `test_no_real_identity_in_the_repository.py`. That test checks shapes and can live in a public repository; a list of forbidden *names* cannot, in any form. A hashed denylist beside the code is an oracle: on 2026-09-09 Ivan inverted 17 of 18 truncated sha256 entries in seconds with a dictionary built from this repository's own history, labels included. So the list is plaintext outside the repository (`~/.config/orbiters/forbidden-names.txt`, overridable with ORBITERS_FORBIDDEN_NAMES) and only this local tier reads it. The scanner prints a notice and exits 0 where no list is configured, which is every machine but ours.

The same file `pigrocrm-py-test` already runs, and here it runs on every diff instead. It lives under projects/pigrocrm but defends the whole tree, so scoping it to that project's paths is how the hub's footer shipped a fixture company's name to production with every gate green (ORB-97). One second, and CI's `identity` job asks the same question on the same file.
